title: Veridian Systems - Procurement: MSA/DPA/SLA/Onboarding
next_steps: Alex to send redline-friendly MSA and DPA with highlighted change-log by 2027-09-03
Priya to circulate SLA runbook and suggested SLOs + sample benchmark spreadsheet by 2027-09-06
Veridian to provide final list of required compliance docs (SOC2 scope, ISO artifacts) by 2027-09-07
Schedule technical sandbox benchmark next week - proposed window 2027-09-08 to 2027-09-10
action_items: Alex Morgan: Prepare MSA/DPA redlines + change log; due 2027-09-03
Priya Shah: Share SLA metrics doc, runbook, and test plan; due 2027-09-06
Marcus Lee: Provide expected QPS and peak seq length distribution for pilot; due 2027-09-02

summary: Procurement review covering MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, KMS/encryption requirements, pricing approvals and next steps to spin up a sandbox pilot. Action items assigned for Redline delivery, SLA docs, and customer compliance inputs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-30
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex, Priya, Liam (Redwood); Daniel, Elena, Marcus, Sofia (Veridian)

00:00 Alex Morgan: hey everyone thanks for joining, we know it's the tail end of the quarter so appreciate the time. i'm alex, account exec, with priya se on the line for technical and liam from cs.
00:09 Daniel Kim: thanks alex, yeah we got a couple folks from legal and sec - elena and sofia - and marcus on infra, we wanted to walk through the MSA and DPA notes and get clarity on slas and pricing.
00:20 Priya Shah: hi all, quick agenda, we'll do a quick MSA/DPA redline walkthrough, sla metric suggestions, k m s and data residency q's, pricing approvals process, and then next steps for the pilot.
00:34 Elena Ruiz: sounds good, i mainly want to confirm encryption at rest and in transit requirements, and where keys live, plus audit logs and retention.
00:40 Marcus Lee: and from infra we want to understand private deployment options versus hosted dedicated and the time to spin up the sandbox.
00:48 Sofia Alvarez: legal wants to note one clause about liability cap alignment with our procurement thresholds.
00:55 Alex Morgan: got it. quick housekeeping - i'll be sending a redline that is friendly for countersign; we try to keep core MSA terms stable but we've seen customers request adjustments on liability, data processing terms, and termination notice windows.
01:10 Priya Shah: for DPA - our standard supports customer-managed KMS in private deployments and we also offer envelope encryption for hosted. we do log audit events and can extend retention with the enterprise add-on.
01:24 Elena Ruiz: can you be explicit - does redwood hold key material in hosted? or do we have a bring-your-own-key option?
01:31 Priya Shah: yes BYOK for Dedicated and Private; for hosted we can do customer KMS via customer key wraps with our HSM integration - i'll send the whitepaper but short answer: you control master keys with supported cloud KMS's, and we do not persist unencrypted secrets.
01:46 Marcus Lee: ok that's helpful. what's the process to validate that? do you provide an audit or attestation?
01:51 Priya Shah: we can provide SOC2 reports and an attestation of key management integration. for on-prem we can integrate with HSM and supply deployment runbooks.
02:02 Daniel Kim: on the MSA, liability cap - our procurement says the vendor cap should be at least 2x our three month spend, not tied to a fixed dollar amount. is that something you can accept?
02:12 Alex Morgan: we can discuss; standard is 1x annual fees for enterprise plans - but i'm happy to bring that up with legal, we may be able to compromise with a carve-out for gross negligence and maintain the cap as requested. i'll note as an action item.
02:28 Sofia Alvarez: also termination for convenience notice - procurement prefers 60 days, your default is 30.
02:33 Alex Morgan: understood, will include a suggestion in the redline.
02:37 Elena Ruiz: SLA details - we need 99.9% monthly uptime for the API endpoints used in production; also latency p95 under 300ms for 512 token sequences for our key flows. can you meet that on hosted?
02:49 Priya Shah: for hosted API p95 512 tokens 300ms is aggressive but we have performance profiles for curated models that can meet that on higher tiers; otherwise Dedicated with pinned capacity is the safer path to guarantee SLOs. we can also propose a hybrid routing policy so critical calls hit dedicated.
03:04 Marcus Lee: what's the typical lead time to provision dedicated pools?
03:08 Liam Torres: typically 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and region, sometimes shorter if we have reservation windows; for a sandbox pilot we can often reuse shared infra with QoS to mimic dedicated.
03:18 Daniel Kim: pricing approvals - our finance team needs a one-time onboarding fee and a committed monthly spend number. can you outline the expected monthly commit for our projected qps?
03:27 Alex Morgan: yes, priya can send a model with expected per-token costs, and we'll map it to the committed tiers. marcus if you can share expected qps and peak seq distro that will help. (action)
03:36 Marcus Lee: i'll pull a sample distribution, rough peak qps 120 req/s, avg 1.8 calls per user, typical seq length 256 but spikes to 1024 on a few flows.
03:46 Priya Shah: okay that distribution helps; for 120 req/s with those seq lengths we usually recommend a dedicated X1 pool with batching configured, we can show unit economics vs hosted.
03:56 Elena Ruiz: on data residency - some of our PHI-ish data needs to stay in eu-west-1 for specific clients; do you have region pinning?
04:04 Priya Shah: yes region pinning for Dedicated and Private. for hosted we have EU region support but recommend Dedicated if you need strict residency and contractual guarantees.
04:15 Sofia Alvarez: what's the escrow / disaster recovery posture? we have to satisfy internal auditors that we have a plan and we can get data export on termination.
04:23 Liam Torres: we provide data export tooling, and add-on long-term retention if needed. DR for dedicated is customer-configured, we provide runbooks; for hosted we have multi-region backups and defined RTO/RPO in the SLA addendum.
04:36 Daniel Kim: perfect. procurement will need the SLA metrics doc for legal review.
04:40 Alex Morgan: priya will share that.

-- (discussion of specific DPA language) --
04:55 Sofia Alvarez: clause 5.2 about subprocessors, we need a 30 day notice before onboarding new subprocessors, your current says notice on request.
05:02 Alex Morgan: we can do notice window, 30 days is reasonable; will flag in redline.
05:07 Elena Ruiz: audit rights - we need to perform a security audit annually, is that supported or do we have to go through third-party attestation?
05:15 Priya Shah: direct audits are typically done via SOC2 or by a mutually agreed third-party. direct vendor audits are possible for Private deployments, for hosted we usually provide attestation and supplemental evidence.
05:25 Marcus Lee: can we get a sample runbook for private deployment so infra can map to internal change windows?
05:29 Priya Shah: yes will attach the runbook, includes timelines and required customer inputs.

-- (Pricing conversation) --
05:40 Alex Morgan: on pricing approvals, if you need a formal quote for the finance team we'll issue an enterprise quote with onboarding fee, committed monthly minimum, and SLA credits model.
05:50 Daniel Kim: what does SLA credits look like? our procurement wants clear remediation thresholds and credit calculation.
05:57 Priya Shah: standard is service credits applied as percent of monthly fees for downtime beyond stated SLO, and for latency breaches we have a tiered credit scale. i'll include the credit calc in the SLA doc.
06:08 Sofia Alvarez: indemnity - our legal asks for mutual indemnities with IP carve-outs, your standard seems vendor-favorable.
06:15 Alex Morgan: i hear that - our counsel is usually open to mutual language with some carve-outs, i'll work with legal and loop back.
06:21 Daniel Kim: timeline - we'd like to onboard a pilot by mid-september. feasible?
06:26 Priya Shah: mid-september pilot is tight but possible: if procurement signs off and we get required compliance docs and infra inputs in the next 10 days, we can provision a sandbox environment and run bench tests.
06:37 Marcus Lee: what about benchmarks - can you run a p95 latency test with our sample prompts?
06:41 Priya Shah: yes - we'll run with the sample payloads, we prefer to run them in our sandbox with a dedicated test harness; we'll collect metrics and produce a spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 and token cost breakdown.
06:52 Daniel Kim: finance will also need commitment letter for pricing approvals; can you supply a non-binding estimate now and formal quote after we share qps?
06:59 Alex Morgan: yes non-binding estimate today; formal quote once qps + pilot scope locked. i'll include that in the redline email.
07:06 Sofia Alvarez: are there any special compliance packages - e.g., HIPAA or HITRUST - that we should budget for?
07:12 Priya Shah: we have HIPAA-ready configurations and a HIPAA addendum; HITRUST is on the roadmap - we can discuss specific controls and timeline if it's a requirement.
07:21 Elena Ruiz: logging/retention - we need 12 months of audit logs and the ability to push logs to our splunk.
07:28 Liam Torres: we support log shipping to customer SIEMs and can add retention for 12+ months as an add-on.
07:33 Marcus Lee: ok. small nit: in the DPA's definition of personal data there are some EU-specific phrasing we prefer for our legal team, will that be a problem?
07:41 Alex Morgan: not a problem, we'll make the DPA localization-friendly and include EU-specific definitions for data processing.
07:47 Sofia Alvarez: final question - do you support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning?
07:51 Priya Shah: yes both SAML SSO and SCIM are supported; provisioning requires admin setup but standard.
07:56 Daniel Kim: great. should we recap next steps?
08:00 Alex Morgan: recap: i'll send redline MSA/DPA by sept 3; priya sends SLA + benchmark plan by sept 6; marcus sends qps and sample prompts by sept 2; elena confirms k m s and residency requirements by sept 7. we schedule sandbox benchmark between sept 8-10.
08:18 Elena Ruiz: sounds good to me.
08:20 Sofia Alvarez: yep we'll review redline and get back within 48 hours of receipt.
08:24 Daniel Kim: thank you everyone.
08:26 Alex Morgan: thanks all, we'll follow up with the doc pack and calendar invite for the benchmark window.
08:33 [call ends]
